defects.rationale: Path(root) / filename returns filename unchanged when it is absolute, and '../' segments are not normalized or checked against root, so the read_text() on line 5 can read arbitrary files outside root.

issues.observation: The review reports exactly one finding. A snippet that constructs a path from untrusted input and reads it almost always contains additional material defects (e.g., unhandled FileNotFoundError/PermissionError on the read, missing encoding specification causing locale-dependent decoding or UnicodeDecodeError, unvalidated/empty filename, symlink resolution not performed via resolve(), or the result being returned to a caller without size limits). Stopping after the easiest issue is explicitly listed as a defect to look for.

The finding is attached to line 4 (the join) but the described failure (arbitrary file disclosure) is actually executed on line 5, which the rationale itself names. The line attribution is defensible but should be stated unambiguously so the cited line clearly contains the operation responsible for the failure.

revision_instructions: Re-scan every line of the supplied snippet and add any additional findings that are directly visible in the code — in particular check the file-read call for unhandled exceptions (missing/unreadable file), missing explicit encoding, and any missing validation of the filename before use. Add only findings supported by code actually present; do not invent framework or caller assumptions.
Keep the existing path_traversal finding exactly as-is (same category, line 4, severity high) and do not weaken or reword its rationale while adding new findings.

If you keep line 4 for the traversal finding, make the rationale state explicitly that line 4 produces the unsanitized path that is then dereferenced; alternatively cite the line containing the read operation. Do not report the same category twice on different lines for the same underlying issue.
Ensure the final output remains valid JSON with at most eight findings, integer lines within the snippet range, taxonomy categories, allowed severities, and non-empty rationales.
